world.paranoia.desc: A city where the walls have ears and the ears have names. The Bureau of Public Quiet keeps a file on everyone; to be forgotten is a death, to be remembered is a leash. Smile. Inform. Survive.
paranoia.npc.1.desc: Your mother, who keeps the wireless low and has not spoken your name aloud since the first Purge; she calls you only 'you', and means it.
paranoia.npc.1.l1: Don't write it down. Whatever it is — don't write it down.
paranoia.npc.1.l2: If they ask, you were here, asleep, all night. I'll say it too.
paranoia.npc.2.desc: The Bureau officer assigned to be your friend: he buys the tea, remembers your birthday, and files a report on both.
paranoia.npc.2.l1: Between us — I'm not the one watching you. But someone is.
paranoia.npc.2.l2: Smile when you say it. They photograph the mouth.
paranoia.npc.3.desc: An old forger from the Night Market who taught you that every document contains one lie, and where to find it.
paranoia.npc.3.l1: Paper lies better than people. Learn to read the paper.
paranoia.npc.3.l2: Never forge a face. Faces are remembered. Numbers are not.
paranoia.npc.4.desc: A young deputy auditor promoted twice for denouncing his own uncle; he wants your file as a stepping stone.
paranoia.npc.4.l1: Your record is clean. That's remarkable. That's suspicious.
paranoia.npc.4.l2: I'll be reading your testimony very carefully.
paranoia.npc.5.desc: A records clerk in the Archive who sells small erasures — a name moved, a date softened — for cigarettes and silence.
paranoia.npc.5.l1: Everything can be edited. Nothing can be deleted.
paranoia.npc.5.l2: Come back when no one is standing behind you.
paranoia.npc.6.desc: The woman across the landing, who lends you salt and counts your comings and goings; you are never sure which of the two is the kindness.
paranoia.npc.6.l1: I heard your door at three. I haven't written it down. Yet.
paranoia.npc.6.l2: We all report a little. It's how we stay neighbours.
paranoia.npc.7.desc: A nine-year-old courier who sells what he sees to whoever pays first — usually the Bureau, sometimes you.
paranoia.npc.7.l1: You were at the Cold Docks. I saw. I always see.
paranoia.npc.7.l2: Give me the coin and I'll forget your face for a week.
paranoia.npc.8.desc: A senior auditor grown tired of the lists; he now warns the people he is assigned to break.
paranoia.npc.8.l1: I'm supposed to destroy you. Sit down. I'll tell you how.
paranoia.npc.8.l2: Do not confess to me. Confess to no one. Confessions are filed.
paranoia.npc.9.desc: A radio singer whose ballads carry coded messages to the disappeared, hidden in the rests between notes.
paranoia.npc.9.l1: Listen to the silence, not the song. That's where I put it.
paranoia.npc.9.l2: They've asked me to sing something loyal. I'll sing it wrong.
paranoia.npc.10.desc: The doorman of your building, who decides who is 'not at home' and who is 'expected'; every bribe in the Quarter passes through his hand.
paranoia.npc.10.l1: You had a visitor. I told them you were out. You owe me.
paranoia.npc.10.l2: The ones who come at night don't use the front. Remember that.
paranoia.era.1.desc: The year the wires went into every wall; the city learned that a whisper can travel farther than a shout.
paranoia.era.2.desc: The state made itself transparent and everyone in it visible; there were no secrets left, only things not yet reported.
paranoia.era.3.desc: Neighbours were taken at dawn in alphabetical order; afterward, the street pretended it had never held so many houses.
paranoia.era.4.desc: Terror settled into routine; the interrogations moved indoors, and the city learned to call the silence peace.
paranoia.era.5.desc: Every tenth year, every citizen must account for themselves; the honest and the guilty are filed in the same drawer.
paranoia.era.6.desc: The records froze, then the pipes; the Bureau still watches, but now even the watchers no longer speak.
paranoia.fac.1.desc: The Bureau of Public Quiet: it writes the questions and the answers, and keeps a file on the file.
paranoia.fac.2.desc: The interrogation sublevels beneath the Hub; what enters is a name, what leaves is a signature.
paranoia.fac.3.desc: The informer network of ordinary neighbours, paid in ration coupons and the pleasure of being spared.
paranoia.fac.4.desc: Those struck from the Archive — officially dead, practically dangerous; they meet on the Roofs and trade in unsaid things.
paranoia.fac.5.desc: The censors and archivists who hold a key to every door and every drawer; they do not choose what to censor, only when.
paranoia.reg.1.desc: The administrative heart, a tower of frosted glass where every paper in the city is born and buried.
paranoia.reg.2.desc: The detention warren below the Hub; the corridors are numbered, the doors are not.
paranoia.reg.3.desc: The harbour where the trawlers come in and the unregistered go out; the water keeps what the Bureau discards.
paranoia.reg.4.desc: A black market under dead lamps, dealing in forged passes, ration cards, and other people's memories.
paranoia.reg.5.desc: A residential district of thin walls and thick curtains, where everyone knows everything and says nothing.
paranoia.reg.6.desc: The rooftop paths above the wires, where the Nameless move and the listening aerials cannot follow.
paranoia.reg.7.desc: The registry of every citizen, living, dead, or erased; the smell of paper covers the smell of fear.
paranoia.lore.1.body: They say the first wire was strung by a man who only wanted to hear his daughter sing in the next room. By winter, every wall in the city had one.
paranoia.lore.2.body: He denounced his brother for a sack of flour and was praised in the square. He ate well that winter, and no one in his family ever spoke to him again.
paranoia.lore.3.body: They came for the A's on Monday and the B's on Tuesday. By Friday the street had learned to fold its letters small and answer only to nicknames.
paranoia.lore.4.body: When the interrogations moved indoors, the city breathed easier. That was the trick of it: they gave us a silence, and we called it peace.
paranoia.lore.5.body: There is only one ladder in the Bureau, and it is climbed by standing on other people's names. Ambition is not a sin here; it is a method.
paranoia.lore.6.body: Look not at who is speaking but at who is listening. In the Watchful, the second is always the more dangerous.
paranoia.lore.7.body: Benevolence here is not a gift; it is a refusal. The kindest thing one can do for a friend is to forget his name on purpose.
paranoia.lore.8.body: Above the wires, there is a city the Bureau cannot hear. The Nameless walk it at night and leave no footprints in any file.
paranoia.lore.9.body: Every emigrant knows it: a homeland's silence reveals its weight only once you are beyond the checkpoint and can hear yourself breathe.
paranoia.lore.10.body: At sixty you understand: the Archive does not keep records. It keeps the version of you that other people chose to believe.
paranoia.lore.11.body: In a corner of the Archive hangs half a file with the name burned out: a life, deliberately left blank. Who it belonged to is still a mystery.
paranoia.lore.12.body: The clearer you see the machine, the harder it is to live inside it. The wisest keepers spend their last years pretending to be blind.
paranoia.lore.13.body: Before thirty you must decide which file you belong to: the careful, the careless, or the one that does not exist.
paranoia.lore.14.body: At forty-five the hardest room is the one where you must confess to something you did not do, and mean it well enough to be believed.
paranoia.lore.15.body: She could have reported you. Instead she moved the sugar tin so the searchers would not find the letter beneath it — and never mentioned it again.
paranoia.lore.16.body: Songbird sang the anthem perfectly, and between every line left a pause too long by half a beat. The whole Ward heard it and said nothing. That was the message.
paranoia.fate.1.desc: You will understand the machine better than those who built it, and will spend your life unable either to run it or to leave it.
paranoia.fate.2.desc: You will spend your years grading other people's souls, and will never once be graded gently yourself.
paranoia.fate.3.desc: You will listen at the wall all your life, and hear only your own heartbeat answering.
paranoia.fate.4.desc: Your name will be struck from every record, and you will be more free than anyone who still has one.
paranoia.fate.5.desc: You will be paid for every name you give, until you have sold the whole street, and you will still be poor.
paranoia.fate.6.desc: You will serve two masters so faithfully that neither will ever know which of your faces is real — not even you.
paranoia.we.1.body: For one night every wire in the city hummed with nothing. People whispered in their sleep, unafraid — and by morning the Bureau had a list of everyone who had.
paranoia.we.2.body: The clerks counted the city and found it larger than its records. An entire ward, it seemed, had been living in the margin for years.
paranoia.we.3.body: The Choir of Keys divided over who had the right to burn a file. The dissent was settled by burning the dissenters' files.
paranoia.we.4.body: Every citizen was called to account for themselves in one season. The honest were exhausted; the guilty were promoted.
paranoia.we.5.body: All across the city, doors were locked from the inside at once. No order was given. No one had to give one. That was the night the Watchful understood itself.
paranoia.we.6.body: The records froze, then the pipes, then the tongues. The Bureau still watches — but now even the watchers have stopped speaking.
paranoia.ev.stranger.1.text: A man in a wet coat stops you in the queue outside the Bureau and says he knew your father — before the file was closed. He offers to buy you tea.
paranoia.ev.stranger.1.listen.note: He knows the date of the arrest, which only a clerk could know.
paranoia.ev.stranger.1.turn.note: You leave; his voice follows you: 'Ask them who signed it.'
paranoia.ev.stranger.2.text: A woman just released from the Sublevels finds you at the ration queue. She repeats a cell number, then asks whether you know that name.
paranoia.ev.stranger.2.listen.note: It is your mother's maiden name, which she has not used in years.
paranoia.ev.stranger.2.turn.note: An orderly leads her away — an orderly who was not there a moment ago.
paranoia.ev.stranger.3.text: A boatman with frost in his beard offers to take one passenger across without papers, tonight, no questions — provided the passenger is not you.
paranoia.ev.stranger.3.listen.note: He wants a name, not money. Any name will do.
paranoia.ev.stranger.3.turn.note: He shrugs, and the fog takes him back.
paranoia.ev.stranger.4.text: A clerk follows you out of the reading room and asks, quietly, whether you have ever seen the paper that erases a person. She has one.
paranoia.ev.stranger.4.listen.note: Your own name is already half-erased on it, in pencil.
paranoia.ev.stranger.4.turn.note: They thank you, and file your report under your name too.
paranoia.ev.theft.1.text: Under the dead lamps, a hand lifts your forged ration book while you bargain. The thief is a child, and the book is your only identity that is not yours.
paranoia.ev.theft.1.chase.note: He weeps, and says the Bureau put him up to it.
paranoia.ev.theft.1.yield.note: You spend the month eating less and lying more.
paranoia.ev.theft.2.text: Someone has prised open your door's third lock — the one installed in secret — and taken nothing but the drawer of letters.
paranoia.ev.theft.2.chase.note: He swears he cut three keys. He only ever mentioned one.
paranoia.ev.theft.2.yield.note: You burn the empty drawer, and sleep with the letters' absence.
paranoia.ev.theft.3.text: A file has gone missing from the reading room: the file that proves where you were on the night of the raid.
paranoia.ev.theft.3.chase.note: The trail ends at Clerk Dane's desk, and Dane is not at his desk.
paranoia.ev.theft.3.yield.note: Without the file your alibi stops existing. So does part of you.
paranoia.ev.theft.4.text: Your bag is taken from the dock shed — not the money, only the photographs. Someone in this city is collecting faces.
paranoia.ev.theft.4.chase.note: You find them in a barrel, every pair of eyes neatly cut out.
paranoia.ev.theft.4.yield.note: You go home and try to remember your father's face.
paranoia.ev.illness.1.text: Fever walks the landing; the woman in 4B coughs through the wall all night. The doctor stopped coming three days ago.
paranoia.ev.illness.1.nurse.note: You tend her; the coughing stops. So does the wireless in 4B, forever.
paranoia.ev.illness.1.avoid.note: You keep well, and hear the cart come for her at dawn.
paranoia.ev.illness.2.text: In the hollow where the Nameless sleep, a man burns with fever. A doctor could be bribed down below — for the price of a name.
paranoia.ev.illness.2.nurse.note: He comes and asks no questions, which frightens you more than the fever.
paranoia.ev.illness.2.avoid.note: By morning he is still; you cannot decide whether to report the body.
paranoia.ev.illness.3.text: A guard you know has fallen ill on duty outside the cells. If he is found sick, he will be moved to a place with no name.
paranoia.ev.illness.3.nurse.note: You hide him in the laundry; he owes you a silence larger than any debt.
paranoia.ev.illness.3.avoid.note: You are commended for vigilance, and given his post.
paranoia.ev.illness.4.text: The canteen serves a soup that tastes wrong; by evening half the clerks have fever, and the Bureau wants no record of it.
paranoia.ev.illness.4.nurse.note: She diagnoses poison, then signs the paper that calls it a cold.
paranoia.ev.illness.4.avoid.note: You go hungry and stay well, and both facts are noticed.
paranoia.ev.windfall.1.text: A crate falls off a trawler and floats to your feet: foreign cigarettes, worth a month of rations. No one on the pier is looking.
paranoia.ev.windfall.1.invest.note: You trade the crate for a favour that will come due exactly when you need it.
paranoia.ev.windfall.1.save.note: The smell of tobacco under the floorboards keeps you hopeful.
paranoia.ev.windfall.2.text: A forger overpays you by mistake — a whole extra packet of passes, already stamped and sealed.
paranoia.ev.windfall.2.invest.note: The passes move fast; so does your name, in the wrong mouths.
paranoia.ev.windfall.2.save.note: You burn them, and wonder for years who they were meant for.
paranoia.ev.windfall.3.text: A filing error lands in your lap: your record shows a promotion you never earned, and a salary to match.
paranoia.ev.windfall.3.invest.note: The money arrives; so does an auditor, asking about the promotion.
paranoia.ev.windfall.3.save.note: The clerk who erred is grateful, and now in your debt.
paranoia.ev.windfall.4.text: You find a lost wallet in the Bureau corridor: identity papers, keys, and a note that says, 'if found, destroy.'
paranoia.ev.windfall.4.invest.note: For one week you live as someone else, and you like it.
paranoia.ev.windfall.4.save.note: The owner retrieves it without thanks; you never learn who he was.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.1.text: Your neighbour, who fed your cat during the curfew, is named in a report as your accomplice. The report is in your handwriting — or a very good copy of it.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.1.confront.note: You prove the hand is not yours; she is released, and knows you hesitated first.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.1.plan.note: She is taken at dawn, and your silence is filed as consent.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.2.text: Clerk Dane has sold your file to a rival department. You catch him re-inking the date that made it clean.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.2.confront.note: He does not deny it; he only asks what you have to trade.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.2.plan.note: You copy it and burn the original; now you own the only you that exists.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.3.text: The forger who made your papers kept a spare set — and is offering them, very quietly, to the highest bidder.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.3.confront.note: You break the press and make an enemy who knows your real face.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.3.plan.note: You pay for your own face, and wonder how often you can afford to.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.4.text: Handler Voss, who buys your tea, writes your name in the margin of a list headed 'Priority.' He smiles as he does it.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.4.confront.note: He answers honestly, which is the worst thing he has ever done to you.
paranoia.ev.betrayal.4.plan.note: You smile back and begin, that night, to become forgettable.
paranoia.ev.festival.1.text: The Ward holds its Loyalty Festival: bunting, anthems, and a microphone in the square for anyone who wishes to testify.
paranoia.ev.festival.1.join.note: You sing; your voice is recorded; the recording is filed under your name.
paranoia.ev.festival.1.work.note: You stay in, and a neighbour notes that your window was dark.
paranoia.ev.festival.2.text: The Bureau opens its glass doors for the Anniversary: citizens are invited to walk the corridors and see how well they are governed.
paranoia.ev.festival.2.join.note: You see a room of files, and for one second your own name on a spine.
paranoia.ev.festival.2.work.note: You stay at your desk, and someone notices the empty chair.
paranoia.ev.festival.3.text: The docks light lanterns for the Missing: one flame for every name nobody dares say aloud.
paranoia.ev.festival.3.join.note: You light one for your father; it drifts out and does not come back.
paranoia.ev.festival.3.work.note: You mend nets all night and miss the only honest hour of the year.
paranoia.ev.festival.4.text: On the Roofs the Nameless hold their own festival — no anthems, no cameras, and a rule that no one says a name that appears in any file.
paranoia.ev.festival.4.join.note: For one night you have a face and no name, and it is a relief.
paranoia.ev.festival.4.work.note: You hear the singing above and pretend it is the wind.
paranoia.ev.rumor.1.text: A rumour climbs the stairwell: that you were the one who signed the report on old Marrow. It is false, which will not help you.
paranoia.ev.rumor.1.trace.note: The source is a widow who lost her son; she cannot be punished without becoming a martyr.
paranoia.ev.rumor.1.ignore.note: It burns out, leaving a small scar that everyone can see.
paranoia.ev.rumor.2.text: Someone in the typing pool says you keep a second set of papers. It is true, which is worse.
paranoia.ev.rumor.2.trace.note: You trade a favour for silence, and the favour becomes a hook in you.
paranoia.ev.rumor.2.ignore.note: The typing pool says nothing more; the Bureau says something later.
paranoia.ev.rumor.3.text: The dockers say you refused to help a drowning man. In fact you were not there; in fact someone paid them to say it.
paranoia.ev.rumor.3.trace.note: You learn the rumour was bought and paid for by a name you know.
paranoia.ev.rumor.3.ignore.note: You stop going to the docks, and the sea keeps the story.
paranoia.ev.rumor.4.text: The Market spreads word that your passes are counterfeit. In the Market, a rumour like that is a death sentence for a trade.
paranoia.ev.rumor.4.trace.note: You prove it, and the forger who started the rumour raises his price.
paranoia.ev.rumor.4.ignore.note: You leave the pass trade, and someone else inherits your customers.
paranoia.ev.journey.1.text: There is a gap in the wire three kilometres out, where a person could cross to the next province and become someone with no file at all.
paranoia.ev.journey.1.go.note: You cross and sleep under a foreign sky, nameless and light.
paranoia.ev.journey.1.stay.note: You turn back and tell yourself the province is no better.
paranoia.ev.journey.2.text: A courier route runs the length of the Roofs to a district the Bureau forgot to census. It takes three nights, and silence.
paranoia.ev.journey.2.go.note: You carry a message and return carrying a stranger's thanks.
paranoia.ev.journey.2.stay.note: Someone else runs it, and the message is lost.
paranoia.ev.journey.3.text: A work detail needs volunteers to cross the checkpoint into the exclusion zone and back before dark.
paranoia.ev.journey.3.go.note: You cross, and see the empty houses the file says are occupied.
paranoia.ev.journey.3.stay.note: The detail returns; one of them does not, and no one asks.
paranoia.ev.journey.4.text: A guard offers, for a price, to walk you out of the Sublevels through the laundry tunnel — once, tonight, no returns.
paranoia.ev.journey.4.go.note: You come out into the cold, free, and unable to prove you ever existed.
paranoia.ev.journey.4.stay.note: You stay; the guard shrugs, and by morning he is gone.
paranoia.ev.duel.1.text: A neighbour accuses you publicly of cowardice during the raid — of hiding while others stood. The landing waits for your answer.
paranoia.ev.duel.1.fight.note: You tell the truth, which is that you hid; they respect the honesty and never trust you again.
paranoia.ev.duel.1.decline.note: You walk upstairs, and the landing decides the verdict without you.
paranoia.ev.duel.2.text: At the audit hearing an auditor belittles your testimony and invites you to correct him publicly.
paranoia.ev.duel.2.fight.note: Your file supports you; he is embarrassed, and now your enemy for life.
paranoia.ev.duel.2.decline.note: You say nothing; later they quietly amend your record.
paranoia.ev.duel.3.text: A rival forger challenges your work before the Market, claiming your stamps are clumsy.
paranoia.ev.duel.3.fight.note: You forge a perfect pass in front of the crowd, and the Market remembers your hands.
paranoia.ev.duel.3.decline.note: They call you cautious, and buy elsewhere for a month.
paranoia.ev.duel.4.text: An inspector questions your loyalty before your colleagues and asks, smiling, whether you would denounce your own brother.
paranoia.ev.duel.4.fight.note: You ask when he last saw his; the room goes cold, and he remembers you.
paranoia.ev.duel.4.decline.note: You agree; your colleagues look away, and one of them writes it down.
paranoia.ev.harvest.1.text: The ration store opens once a month. This month the clerk says the count is short, and that someone in the queue has been hoarding.
paranoia.ev.harvest.1.share.note: You give your portion to a family with a sick child, and go home lighter in every way.
paranoia.ev.harvest.1.hoard.note: You take your full share and lock the door, and the queue remembers.
paranoia.ev.harvest.2.text: The rooftop plots have yielded a few hard vegetables. The Nameless divide them by a rule older than the Bureau: the weakest eat first.
paranoia.ev.harvest.2.share.note: You take the smallest portion and gain the only trust that costs nothing.
paranoia.ev.harvest.2.hoard.note: You take more; no one stops you, and no one speaks to you again.
paranoia.ev.harvest.3.text: The trawler brings in a good catch, and the dock boss will share with those who helped haul — but the list of helpers is also a list of names.
paranoia.ev.harvest.3.share.note: Your name is on the haul list, and on a Bureau desk by morning.
paranoia.ev.harvest.3.hoard.note: You help without a name and take fish without a record.
paranoia.ev.harvest.4.text: The Bureau distributes surplus grain as a gift from the state, with a form to sign acknowledging receipt and gratitude.
paranoia.ev.harvest.4.share.note: You sign, and the grain feeds you; the signature feeds the file.
paranoia.ev.harvest.4.hoard.note: You refuse, and are marked as a citizen who does not need the state.
paranoia.ev.law.1.text: The Bureau decrees that every citizen must report any change of address within one day, on pain of being struck from the ration rolls.
paranoia.ev.law.1.obey.note: You queue three hours to tell them what they already knew.
paranoia.ev.law.1.defy.note: They knew anyway; the fine arrives before you do.
paranoia.ev.law.2.text: A curfew is declared, beginning an hour before dark: no lights, no wireless, no footsteps on the landing.
paranoia.ev.law.2.obey.note: You sit in the dark and hear your own breathing as a stranger's.
paranoia.ev.law.2.defy.note: The lamp is seen; the fine is doubled for a second offence.
paranoia.ev.law.3.text: All passes must now carry a photograph. The Market's forgers can print numbers but not faces.
paranoia.ev.law.3.obey.note: Your face enters the system of faces, and cannot be taken back.
paranoia.ev.law.3.defy.note: You wear another's face until it is missed.
paranoia.ev.law.4.text: The Archive announces that records older than ten years will be consolidated — which is to say, most people's childhoods will be destroyed.
paranoia.ev.law.4.obey.note: You watch a clerk feed the faded pages into the furnace.
paranoia.ev.law.4.defy.note: You copy your childhood into a drainpipe, and hope the paper outlives you.
paranoia.ev.first_love.1.text: A new tenant moves into the flat below, laughs too loudly, and invites you in for tea on the first night.
paranoia.ev.first_love.1.woo.note: By morning you know each other's real names, which is a risk you now share.
paranoia.ev.first_love.1.friend.note: You keep the doorstep between you, and become the one person they trust.
paranoia.ev.first_love.2.text: The courier who brings your papers has a face you begin to look for in the crowd — and a name you are never given.
paranoia.ev.first_love.2.woo.note: They give you a false one, and you both pretend to believe it.
paranoia.ev.first_love.2.friend.note: You memorize their footsteps; it is a kind of love that keeps you both alive.
paranoia.ev.first_love.3.text: On the Roofs you meet someone who also comes up to be nameless. You share the cold and a cigarette most nights.
paranoia.ev.first_love.3.woo.note: You trade names, the most dangerous gift either of you owns.
paranoia.ev.first_love.3.friend.note: You never learn who they are, and it is the only honest thing between you.
paranoia.ev.first_love.4.text: Between the stacks a clerk passes you a note that is not about work: it asks whether you are free tonight.
paranoia.ev.first_love.4.woo.note: You meet after hours, and the silence of the reading room is the only witness.
paranoia.ev.first_love.4.friend.note: You return the note, and never learn what they wanted to say.
paranoia.ev.grief.1.text: A man you knew from the canteen is reported dead in the Sublevels. No cause is given, and the body is not returned.
paranoia.ev.grief.1.mourn.note: You light one in the window; by morning the window has been photographed.
paranoia.ev.grief.1.carry.note: You take a double shift and refuse to think about the Sublevels.
paranoia.ev.grief.2.text: The woman in 4B is gone; the cart came at dawn, and her flat is already being repainted for the next tenant.
paranoia.ev.grief.2.mourn.note: You say the name she never said aloud, and the landing pretends not to hear.
paranoia.ev.grief.2.carry.note: You help paint over her life, and the landlord remembers you kindly.
paranoia.ev.grief.3.text: A trawlerman did not come back; his boots are on the pier, and the sea is the only record of him now.
paranoia.ev.grief.3.mourn.note: You throw them into the grey water and watch them go where he went.
paranoia.ev.grief.3.carry.note: You wear them; they fit, and you tell no one.
paranoia.ev.grief.4.text: One of the Nameless has died up here, quietly, of cold. The custom is to leave the body for the Bureau to find.
paranoia.ev.grief.4.mourn.note: You sit with the body until dawn, and learn the face no file will hold.
paranoia.ev.grief.4.carry.note: You move on with the others, carrying his silence in your own.
paranoia.ev.craft.1.text: The old forger Weasel offers to teach you his art — the reading of a false document, and the making of one.
paranoia.ev.craft.1.take.note: You learn to make a pass that fools anyone but Weasel.
paranoia.ev.craft.1.refuse.note: You decline, and your hands stay clean and your pockets thin.
paranoia.ev.craft.2.text: A courier needs a partner for a run across the Roofs: two people, one message, twice the chance of one surviving.
paranoia.ev.craft.2.take.note: You learn every rooftop in the Ward, and the sound of footsteps not following you.
paranoia.ev.craft.2.refuse.note: The courier runs alone, and comes back alone.
paranoia.ev.craft.3.text: A boatman will teach you the fog channel — for a fee, and a promise never to use it for anyone but yourself.
paranoia.ev.craft.3.take.note: You can now leave the city by water, whenever you choose.
paranoia.ev.craft.3.refuse.note: You keep your boots dry and your options few.
paranoia.ev.craft.4.text: An archivist offers to show you how the filing system thinks — how a name is moved from one drawer to another.
paranoia.ev.craft.4.take.note: You learn the grammar of the Archive, and can now write in it.
paranoia.ev.craft.4.refuse.note: You stay a reader all your life, and never a writer.
paranoia.ev.secret.1.text: In the margins of a file you find a note in your mother's hand, addressed to someone whose name has been torn away.
paranoia.ev.secret.1.open.note: She burns it unread, and does not speak to you for a week.
paranoia.ev.secret.1.leave.note: You leave it where it was, and it is gone by morning.
paranoia.ev.secret.2.text: Through the wall you hear your neighbour rehearsing a denunciation — of you. She practises it aloud, at night, in a steady voice.
paranoia.ev.secret.2.open.note: She weeps and admits it; you are both now bound by her weakness.
paranoia.ev.secret.2.leave.note: You hear it every night for a month, and sleep less each time.
paranoia.ev.secret.3.text: A friend in the typing pool shows you a carbon copy of an order to search your flat — dated tomorrow.
paranoia.ev.secret.3.open.note: Two escape, one does not, and the one who does not knows your name.
paranoia.ev.secret.3.leave.note: The searchers find only dust, and dust is not evidence.
paranoia.ev.secret.4.text: A guard you bribed says a prisoner in the cells is asking for you by a name only your family uses.
paranoia.ev.secret.4.open.note: It is your uncle, whom the records say died in the Purge.
paranoia.ev.secret.4.leave.note: You send nothing, and the asking stops within the week.
paranoia.ev.drought.1.text: The water rations are halved; the pipes run dry by noon, and neighbours queue at the one working tap in the courtyard.
paranoia.ev.drought.1.ration.note: You queue three hours for a bucket, and share it with the old man behind you.
paranoia.ev.drought.1.take.note: You steal water in the dark, and the dry taps are reported by morning.
paranoia.ev.drought.2.text: No rain for a month; the rooftop cisterns are down to mud, and the Nameless guard the last of the water.
paranoia.ev.drought.2.ration.note: You take a shift at the cistern and earn the right to drink.
paranoia.ev.drought.2.take.note: No one sees you — but everyone counts.
paranoia.ev.drought.3.text: Fresh water is brought in by boat and sold at the pier; the price rises with every hour of thirst.
paranoia.ev.drought.3.ration.note: You buy just enough, and learn the taste of restraint.
paranoia.ev.drought.3.take.note: You become, overnight, a person others visit at night.
paranoia.ev.drought.4.text: The Bureau closes the public fountains and reserves the water for its own clerks — who are, it reminds you, the state.
paranoia.ev.drought.4.ration.note: You drink from the trickle in your own sink and say nothing.
paranoia.ev.drought.4.take.note: The ward drinks in the night; by morning the guards are looking for a culprit.
paranoia.ev.gift.1.text: A stranger on the Roofs leaves a tin of real coffee at your usual spot, with no note.
paranoia.ev.gift.1.accept.note: The coffee is real and the kindness is real, and you never learn the giver.
paranoia.ev.gift.1.suspect.note: By morning it is gone, and you wonder about it for a year.
paranoia.ev.gift.2.text: A vendor slips an extra stamp into your change and closes your hand over it.
paranoia.ev.gift.2.accept.note: The stamp buys you a week of not being asked questions.
paranoia.ev.gift.2.suspect.note: The vendor looks at you as though you have failed a test.
paranoia.ev.gift.3.text: An anonymous package arrives at your desk: a bar of chocolate, from a colleague careful enough not to sign it.
paranoia.ev.gift.3.accept.note: You eat half and save half; the saved half carries you through the bad night.
paranoia.ev.gift.3.suspect.note: It tests clean; the colleague never speaks to you again.
paranoia.ev.gift.4.text: The neighbour you distrust leaves a parcel at your door: your letters, the ones taken from the drawer, every one unread.
paranoia.ev.gift.4.accept.note: You thank her; something between you changes for the better, and stays changed.
paranoia.ev.gift.4.suspect.note: One is missing. You spend the winter wondering which.
paranoia.ev.war.1.text: War comes to the border; the checkpoints are doubled, and the Bureau begins conscripting clerks into the People's Militia.
paranoia.ev.war.1.serve.note: You are drilled, armed, and sent to guard a wire you once crossed to escape.
paranoia.ev.war.1.hide.note: You limp through the war in a records office, hating yourself usefully.
paranoia.ev.war.2.text: The militia sweeps the Roofs for deserters; the Nameless have nowhere left to go but down.
paranoia.ev.war.2.serve.note: They take three; you never sleep in the same place again.
paranoia.ev.war.2.hide.note: You hide two under your floor until the sweep passes, and the streets above grow quiet.
paranoia.ev.war.3.text: The port is requisitioned; private boats are seized, and anyone with a boat is a person of interest.
paranoia.ev.war.3.serve.note: You hand over the keys and are thanked by a man who never learns your name.
paranoia.ev.war.3.hide.note: You sink it in the shallows, to raise after the war — if there is an after.
paranoia.ev.war.4.text: The Bureau demands volunteers to sort the war's paper: lists of the dead, the missing, and the merely inconvenient.
paranoia.ev.war.4.serve.note: You sort the lists and learn exactly how a person is crossed out.
paranoia.ev.war.4.hide.note: You are sick with something they cannot name, and are left alone for a month.
paranoia.ev.famine.1.text: Hunger has moved into the Ward; the ration is half a loaf, and the queue grows longer as the loaf grows smaller.
paranoia.ev.famine.1.share.note: You give half to the woman with the child, and sleep with the good kind of emptiness.
paranoia.ev.famine.1.close.note: You hear her crying through the wall and chew more slowly.
paranoia.ev.famine.2.text: The Bureau announces an austerity measure: clerks will eat last, after the state's guests.
paranoia.ev.famine.2.share.note: You and three others share everything; it tastes of solidarity and is nearly enough.
paranoia.ev.famine.2.close.note: Your food is locked in your drawer, and the drawer is broken into by Friday.
paranoia.ev.famine.3.text: The Nameless are starving; they have begun eating what the city throws out, and the city has begun watching.
paranoia.ev.famine.3.share.note: You carry bread up the fire escape for a month, and never once say why.
paranoia.ev.famine.3.close.note: You stop climbing; one of them, you later hear, is gone before spring.
paranoia.ev.famine.4.text: In the cells the guards eat and the prisoners do not. A guard offers you an extra portion to look away while he empties a bowl.
paranoia.ev.famine.4.share.note: You pass your own bread through the bars; the guard reports you for waste.
paranoia.ev.famine.4.close.note: You eat it, and it is the heaviest meal of your life.
paranoia.ev.tradition.1.text: The Bureau revives an old rite: all citizens must renew their oath of loyalty aloud, in the square, on the anniversary.
paranoia.ev.tradition.1.keep.note: You swear it in a clear voice, and the clear voice is recorded.
paranoia.ev.tradition.1.break.note: A neighbour reports the mumble; you are asked to repeat it privately.
paranoia.ev.tradition.2.text: An old custom returns: on the first frost, each household burns a paper bearing the name of a fear, so the year may pass.
paranoia.ev.tradition.2.keep.note: You write a name and burn it; the year passes, and the name does not.
paranoia.ev.tradition.2.break.note: The neighbours burn two papers that night, and one of them is yours.
paranoia.ev.tradition.3.text: The archivists mark the Day of Silence: for one hour at noon, every file is closed and every clerk stands still.
paranoia.ev.tradition.3.keep.note: You stand in the silence and hear the building breathe around you.
paranoia.ev.tradition.3.break.note: You read through the hour, and learn something the silence was meant to hide.
paranoia.ev.tradition.4.text: The dockers keep an older rite than the Bureau's: a lantern is set adrift for each boat that did not come back, and no one speaks its name.
paranoia.ev.tradition.4.keep.note: You set one adrift and keep the name in your mouth.
paranoia.ev.tradition.4.break.note: You say it aloud; the dockers look at you as though you had opened a grave.
paranoia.ev.legacy.1.text: An archivist asks what you want done with your file after you die: keep it, close it, or erase it entirely.
paranoia.ev.legacy.1.write.note: You write that the file should be burned; the instruction goes into the file.
paranoia.ev.legacy.1.silent.note: The file will outlive you and, like you, say nothing.
paranoia.ev.legacy.2.text: A young courier asks you to teach the routes — the ones that are written on no map.
paranoia.ev.legacy.2.write.note: You walk the Roofs one last time with them, naming every ledge.
paranoia.ev.legacy.2.silent.note: You teach the route to your own door, and keep the rest.
paranoia.ev.legacy.3.text: Your neighbour asks you to witness her will — a single line leaving everything to a niece whose name she will not say aloud.
paranoia.ev.legacy.3.write.note: You sign, and the niece's name never enters a record but your memory.
paranoia.ev.legacy.3.silent.note: She finds another witness, and the line is lost.
paranoia.ev.legacy.4.text: The Bureau offers to buy your testimony at the end, for the archive of the Watchful — a small pension for your heirs.
paranoia.ev.legacy.4.write.note: You tell them everything; your heirs eat, and your name becomes a lesson.
paranoia.ev.legacy.4.silent.note: Your heirs go hungry, and your name stays yours.
paranoia.ev.temptation.1.text: A Bureau officer offers you a promotion, a larger flat, and a car — for one signature, denouncing a colleague you barely know.
paranoia.ev.temptation.1.resist.note: He smiles as he leaves, and your file gains a note about your softness.
paranoia.ev.temptation.1.yield.note: The flat is warm; the colleague is gone by Friday.
paranoia.ev.temptation.2.text: A forger offers to make you a brand-new identity — papers, past, even a family — enough to leave the old you behind forever.
paranoia.ev.temptation.2.resist.note: You keep it, and wonder some nights whether that was wisdom or cowardice.
paranoia.ev.temptation.2.yield.note: You become a stranger with your own memories, and no one comes looking.
paranoia.ev.temptation.3.text: A guard offers to lose your interrogation file — if you will name one other prisoner who talked.
paranoia.ev.temptation.3.resist.note: You refuse, and the interrogation goes on another week.
paranoia.ev.temptation.3.yield.note: The file disappears, and so does he.
paranoia.ev.temptation.4.text: A neighbour offers a place on the evacuation list for you and yours — if you report the family in 4B, who have no papers.
paranoia.ev.temptation.4.resist.note: The raid takes your household rather than theirs.
paranoia.ev.temptation.4.yield.note: You get the place; the family in 4B is taken at dawn.
paranoia.ev.rescue.1.text: A man goes into the water at the docks at night. The dockers on the pier are not moving; the water is below freezing.
paranoia.ev.rescue.1.help.note: You pull him out, half-frozen; both live, and both are now witnesses.
paranoia.ev.rescue.1.pass.note: The watch arrives too late, and the dockers remember that you called them.
paranoia.ev.rescue.2.text: Smoke comes from under the door of 4B; the fire brigade will not enter a building under suspicion without an order.
paranoia.ev.rescue.2.help.note: You pull out the children; the fire is called arson, and arson needs a culprit.
paranoia.ev.rescue.2.pass.note: The order comes in an hour; by then the family is quiet.
paranoia.ev.rescue.3.text: A Nameless courier is cornered by the militia on a roof with no exit but the drop.
paranoia.ev.rescue.3.help.note: They vanish into the dark; the militia notes a loose grate.
paranoia.ev.rescue.3.pass.note: You walk on; behind you the roof goes silent.
paranoia.ev.rescue.4.text: A prisoner is being beaten in the corridor. A guard you know looks at you and shrugs, as if to say, it is your choice.
paranoia.ev.rescue.4.help.note: The prisoner lives, and the guard now knows a weakness of yours.
paranoia.ev.rescue.4.pass.note: The beating stops at dawn, and the sound does not.
paranoia.ev.bargain.1.text: A dealer offers your own stolen letters back — no price named, only a question: what are they worth to you, in favours?
paranoia.ev.bargain.1.deal.note: You buy them back with a promise you cannot afford to keep.
paranoia.ev.bargain.1.walk.note: The letters are sold to someone who reads them aloud.
paranoia.ev.bargain.2.text: A captain offers to carry a passenger out on tonight's tide for half price — if you will vouch for the passenger to the Bureau.
paranoia.ev.bargain.2.deal.note: The boat leaves, and your name is now attached to a departure.
paranoia.ev.bargain.2.walk.note: The passenger stays, and looks at you every day.
paranoia.ev.bargain.3.text: Clerk Dane offers to change your record so your father's arrest reads as 'natural causes' — for a fee, and a favour to be named later.
paranoia.ev.bargain.3.deal.note: You owe a favour that will one day be called in.
paranoia.ev.bargain.3.walk.note: You leave the record as it is, and learn to live with the exact truth.
paranoia.ev.bargain.4.text: An auditor offers to lose your file entirely — for a sum you have, and a name you do not wish to give.
paranoia.ev.bargain.4.deal.note: Your file is lost; so, soon after, is the person whose name you gave.
paranoia.ev.bargain.4.walk.note: You keep it, and your file stays exactly where it is.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.1.text: A storm tears the aerials off the roofs, and for one night the listening posts are blind. The Nameless want to move everything while they can.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.1.shelter.note: You carry the Nameless and their papers across the roofs, and the storm covers you.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.1.self.note: You listen to the wind and do nothing, and the chance passes.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.2.text: A storm closes the port; a boat in the roads signals for help, and no one on shore is willing to be seen launching.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.2.shelter.note: You row out and bring in two survivors who owe you a silence.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.2.self.note: You bar the door and listen to the signal fail.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.3.text: The wind takes the power out across the Ward; in the dark, someone knocks at your door and will not give a name.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.3.shelter.note: You shelter a soaked stranger until dawn; they leave without a word.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.3.self.note: The knocking stops; in the morning there is blood on the doorstep.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.4.text: The storm floods the Hub's basement, where the oldest records are kept. The Bureau wants volunteers, and is watching who refuses.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.4.shelter.note: Some files are saved, and some are saved by being lost.
paranoia.ev.storm_night.4.self.note: Your absence is recorded in a file that survived.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.1.text: The Archive opens a course in record-keeping; attendance is mandatory, and so is the loyalty examination at the end.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.1.study.note: You pass, and are offered a desk in the department that watches you.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.1.play.note: You scrape by; the examiner writes, 'attitude: insufficient.'
paranoia.ev.scholarship.2.text: A senior clerk offers private lessons in the Bureau's real grammar — what the euphemisms actually order.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.2.study.note: You learn to read orders as they are meant, and cannot unlearn it.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.2.play.note: You remain a person who believes what he is told, and sleep better.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.3.text: A forger will teach you to copy any hand, including your own — for a price that includes a sample of your signature.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.3.study.note: You wonder forever what your signature has been used for.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.3.play.note: You keep your signature out of the Market, and your safety.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.4.text: The Nameless keep an older knowledge: how to read the city by its sounds, and know when a sweep is coming.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.4.study.note: You learn to hear a raid an hour before it arrives.
paranoia.ev.scholarship.4.play.note: You trust your eyes, and are surprised exactly once.
paranoia.ev.honor.1.text: The Bureau names you Employee of the Quarter and hangs your photograph on the wall — where everyone can study your face.
paranoia.ev.honor.1.accept.note: Your face hangs in the corridor; you avoid walking past it.
paranoia.ev.honor.1.decline.note: They accept your decline, and make a note of it.
paranoia.ev.honor.2.text: The archivists nominate you Keeper of the Keys — a title with no power and every door.
paranoia.ev.honor.2.accept.note: You hold the keys to every drawer, and never open your own.
paranoia.ev.honor.2.decline.note: They go to someone who will use them, and you are watched for the refusal.
paranoia.ev.honor.3.text: The Ward proposes to name a courtyard after your family — if you will consent to a plaque bearing the state's motto.
paranoia.ev.honor.3.accept.note: The courtyard bears your name and the motto, and the neighbours stop using both.
paranoia.ev.honor.3.decline.note: There is no plaque; the courtyard keeps its old, unsaid name.
paranoia.ev.honor.4.text: The warden offers to make you a trustee: a prisoner with keys, trusted to keep order and to report.
paranoia.ev.honor.4.accept.note: The other prisoners stop meeting your eyes.
paranoia.ev.honor.4.decline.note: You are returned to the general population, where nobody trusts you either.
paranoia.ev.lost.1.text: You lose your way on the Roofs after curfew, in a part of the city that has no street names and no lamps.
paranoia.ev.lost.1.call.note: A light answers from a chimney; a Nameless guide leads you down.
paranoia.ev.lost.1.wait.note: You wait, cold and quiet, and dawn finds you a hundred metres from home.
paranoia.ev.lost.2.text: You take a wrong turn in the Sublevels and find a corridor not on the plan, ending at a door with no number.
paranoia.ev.lost.2.call.note: The door opens inward; a clerk you have never seen asks what you want filed.
paranoia.ev.lost.2.wait.note: You find your way back; the corridor is gone from the plan next day.
paranoia.ev.lost.3.text: In the fog at the docks you lose the pier, and the sound of water is suddenly on every side.
paranoia.ev.lost.3.call.note: A boatman's voice answers and talks you back to shore.
paranoia.ev.lost.3.wait.note: You stand until the fog lifts, and see how close you came.
paranoia.ev.lost.4.text: The Market's lanes shift at night; you lose the door you came in by, and the lamps are going out.
paranoia.ev.lost.4.call.note: A vendor points the way, and charges you for the answer.
paranoia.ev.lost.4.wait.note: You follow the crowd out and end up somewhere you did not intend.
paranoia.ev.dream.1.text: You dream that the wall has stopped listening, and wake to find the wall exactly as it was.
paranoia.ev.dream.1.follow.note: You write the dream on a scrap and burn it, just in case.
paranoia.ev.dream.1.wake.note: You shake it off; the wall ticks softly, listening.
paranoia.ev.dream.2.text: You dream of a cell with your name on the door, and a key in your own pocket.
paranoia.ev.dream.2.follow.note: You wake with your hand at your pocket, and something hard inside.
paranoia.ev.dream.2.wake.note: You call it a dream, and the pocket holds only lint.
paranoia.ev.dream.3.text: You dream of walking the roofs with your father, who has been erased, and he is telling you where the file is kept.
paranoia.ev.dream.3.follow.note: You wake and go where the dream said; there is a drawer, and it is empty.
paranoia.ev.dream.3.wake.note: The dream returns every winter, a little fainter.
paranoia.ev.dream.4.text: You dream that you are a file, being read aloud to a room of people who can change you at will.
paranoia.ev.dream.4.follow.note: You wake and read your own file cover to cover.
paranoia.ev.dream.4.wake.note: You forget the dream, the room, and the changes.
paranoia.ev.bet.1.text: A dealer bets you cannot forge a Bureau seal good enough to fool an inspector.
paranoia.ev.bet.1.match.note: You forge it; the inspector passes; the Market remembers your hands.
paranoia.ev.bet.1.fold.note: The dealer tells the story anyway, with you in it.
paranoia.ev.bet.2.text: Colleagues bet on who will be promoted first; the stakes are cigarettes, and the winner will be whoever reports the most.
paranoia.ev.bet.2.match.note: By month's end you know exactly what a colleague's silence costs.
paranoia.ev.bet.2.fold.note: The pool is taken, and you are on nobody's list.
paranoia.ev.bet.3.text: The Nameless bet you cannot cross the whole city on the rooftops in one night without touching a street.
paranoia.ev.bet.3.match.note: You do it by dawn, and are given a name that appears in no file.
paranoia.ev.bet.3.fold: Keep your feet on the ground
paranoia.ev.bet.3.fold.note: You sleep the deep sleep of the obedient.
paranoia.ev.bet.4.text: The dockers bet on when the next boat will be seized; the nearest guess takes the pool.
paranoia.ev.bet.4.match.note: You guess right and collect; the boat is seized on schedule.
paranoia.ev.bet.4.fold.note: The boats keep going out without you.
paranoia.ev.hermit.1.text: An old man lives on the Roofs in a shack of tin and antennae; they say he used to write the lists, and stopped.
paranoia.ev.hermit.1.learn.note: He teaches you which names on a list matter, and which are only bait.
paranoia.ev.hermit.1.mock.note: You leave; his laughter follows you down the ladder.
paranoia.ev.hermit.2.text: A blind woman keeps a lamp at the end of the pier and asks every passer-by for a name no one will give.
paranoia.ev.hermit.2.learn.note: You give her your own; she says it back, and you feel, briefly, real.
paranoia.ev.hermit.2.mock.note: You refuse; she keeps the lamp lit all night anyway.
paranoia.ev.hermit.3.text: In the closed section of the Archive sits a clerk who has read every file and speaks to no one.
paranoia.ev.hermit.3.learn.note: He says only: 'Everyone is innocent on the first page of their file.'
paranoia.ev.hermit.3.mock.note: You dismiss him; years later you finally understand the sentence.
paranoia.ev.hermit.4.text: A woman in the Ward has not left her flat since the Purge; she speaks to visitors through the door.
paranoia.ev.hermit.4.learn.note: She tells you who informed on whom, and how she knows.
paranoia.ev.hermit.4.mock.note: The door stays shut, and the flat becomes a legend.
paranoia.ev.quiet.text: For once the stairwell is silent, the wireless plays something gentle, and no one knocks.
paranoia.ev.omen.text: A white bird lands on the antenna outside your window and stays a while.
paranoia.ev.hard.text: The queues are long, the forms are wrong, and every official knows your name for the wrong reason.
paranoia.ev.dread.text: Nothing has happened. That, in this city, is never nothing.
paranoia.ev.bounty.text: An old debt is repaid in an envelope on your doormat, unmarked and unexpected.
paranoia.ev.weariness.text: You sit with your boots on and cannot remember which fear you are supposed to be feeling.
paranoia.beh.care.1: Re-dresses the wound beneath your coat
paranoia.beh.care.1.res: Your wound is bound, and the binding hidden.
paranoia.beh.care.2: Sits with you until the patrol passes
paranoia.beh.care.2.res: Someone sat with you in the dark until the footsteps went away.
paranoia.beh.care.3.res: The evidence went into the stove, and so did the smell.
paranoia.beh.meal.1: Saves you half a ration tin
paranoia.beh.meal.1.res: Half a tin of fish, eaten in the dark, tasting of trust.
paranoia.beh.meal.2: Shares a bowl from the canteen
paranoia.beh.meal.2.res: You ate from another's bowl and did not ask what was in it.
paranoia.beh.meal.3.res: A meal in a curtained room; no one said a word that mattered.
paranoia.beh.coin.1.res: Coupons in your palm, warm from another's pocket.
paranoia.beh.coin.2: Settles your fine at the Bureau window
paranoia.beh.coin.2.res: A debt was paid quietly in your name.
paranoia.beh.coin.3: Buys your silence with a fold of notes
paranoia.beh.coin.3.res: Money for forgetting — yours to spend, and to remember.
paranoia.beh.talk.1: Talks of the weather, meaning the patrols
paranoia.beh.talk.1.res: You learned where the patrols walk, and called it weather.
paranoia.beh.talk.2: Whispers a coded rumour over tea
paranoia.beh.talk.2.res: A rumour, wrapped in small talk, reached you intact.
paranoia.beh.talk.3: Talks all night so the wire hears nothing
paranoia.beh.talk.3.res: You spoke all night of nothing, and the wire learned nothing.
paranoia.beh.teach.1: Teaches you to read a forged stamp
paranoia.beh.teach.1.res: You can now spot a Bureau forgery at a glance.
paranoia.beh.teach.2: Shows you the corner where the wire hides
paranoia.beh.teach.2.res: You know which corner of every room lies.
paranoia.beh.teach.3.res: A map of Roofs and drains you will never forget.
paranoia.beh.train.1: Walks the Roofs with you after curfew
paranoia.beh.train.1.res: Your legs learned the paths above the wires.
paranoia.beh.train.2: Trains you to take a blow in silence
paranoia.beh.train.2.res: You can be struck, and stay quiet.
paranoia.beh.train.3: Teaches you to vanish in a crowd
paranoia.beh.train.3.res: You learned to be one of many, and to be no one.
paranoia.beh.warn.1: Warns you your name is on a list
paranoia.beh.warn.1.res: You burned the note, but the list stays in your head.
paranoia.beh.warn.2: Signs a warning to you in the street
paranoia.beh.warn.2.res: A hand-sign said: not tonight. You went home the long way.
paranoia.beh.warn.3: Tells you which neighbour to distrust
paranoia.beh.warn.3.res: You now distrust exactly one person, and watch all the rest.
paranoia.beh.gift.1.res: A pass with your face and another name; it will open one door.
paranoia.beh.gift.2.res: A whole second self, on paper, waiting to be used.
paranoia.beh.gift.3: Gives you a key with no address
paranoia.beh.gift.3.res: A key without a lock; you keep it, and wonder.
paranoia.beh.song.1: Hums the loyal march, deliberately off-key
paranoia.beh.song.1.res: The wrong note said: I am still one of you.
paranoia.beh.song.2: Sings the banned verse under the anthem
paranoia.beh.song.2.res: You heard the banned verse, and did not applaud.
paranoia.beh.song.3: Sings your real name between the notes
paranoia.beh.song.3.res: Someone sang your name in a place that keeps no records.
paranoia.beh.rest.1: Watches the door while you sleep
paranoia.beh.rest.1.res: You slept; they watched. It was the best sleep in years.
paranoia.beh.rest.2: Turns up the radio to cover your nightmares
paranoia.beh.rest.2.res: Static covered your screaming; no one came.
paranoia.beh.rest.3: Tells you to sleep, and lies about the hour
paranoia.beh.rest.3.res: You slept past curfew, and were told it was early.
paranoia.beh.debt.1: Borrows coupons and repays them doubled
paranoia.beh.debt.1.res: A debt repaid twice — a kindness, or a leash.
paranoia.beh.debt.2: Asks you to carry a parcel and not look
paranoia.beh.debt.2.res: Your bag is heavier; your curiosity is not.
paranoia.beh.debt.3: Makes you owe the Bureau a favour
paranoia.beh.debt.3.res: You are now owned by, and owe, the wrong people.
paranoia.beh.rumor.1: Whispers your name into the wrong ear
paranoia.beh.rumor.1.res: Your name reached the Bureau before you did.
paranoia.beh.rumor.2: Spreads that you informed on your own street
paranoia.beh.rumor.2.res: The street looks at you differently now.
paranoia.beh.rumor.3: Files a report and calls it concern
paranoia.beh.rumor.3.res: A report, written in kindness, is still a report.
paranoia.beh.taunt.1: Mocks your fear of the wire
paranoia.beh.taunt.1.res: A jeer, loud enough for the microphone.
paranoia.beh.taunt.2: Calls you a coward before the neighbours
paranoia.beh.taunt.2.res: The landing heard; the landing remembers.
paranoia.beh.taunt.3.res: They laughed at the gap in your file.
paranoia.beh.scheme.1: Moves your name up the audit list
paranoia.beh.scheme.1.res: Your audit came early, and your answers were not ready.
paranoia.beh.scheme.2.res: Your book is gone, and your appetite is watched.
paranoia.beh.scheme.3: Reports you as a foreign sympathiser
paranoia.beh.scheme.3.res: The charge is absurd; absurd charges stick.
paranoia.beh.upkeep.1: Puts in a good word with the doorman
paranoia.beh.upkeep.1.res: For a week you are 'expected', not 'away'.
paranoia.beh.upkeep.2: Has your file mislaid for a month
paranoia.beh.upkeep.2.res: A month of being forgotten — a gift beyond price.
paranoia.beh.upkeep.3: Arranges your transfer off the night list
paranoia.beh.upkeep.3.res: Your name left the night list; you never asked how.
paranoia.off.visit.1.text: They ask you to come by after dark, saying only that the tea is bad and the walls are thin. Go?
paranoia.off.visit.1.yes.res: You drank bad tea and heard one true thing.
paranoia.off.visit.1.no.res: They accepted too quickly, and you wondered for a week.
paranoia.off.visit.2: Invites you to a sealed supper
paranoia.off.visit.2.text: An invitation to a private supper, sealed with wax, in a house with too few windows. Attend?
paranoia.off.visit.2.yes.res: Three guests; one of them was recording.
paranoia.off.visit.2.no.res: You stayed home; someone watched the house all evening.
paranoia.off.favor.1.text: They ask you to carry a parcel across the Ward and not to ask what is inside. Carry it?
paranoia.off.favor.1.yes.res: You carried it, and never learned what you carried.
paranoia.off.favor.1.no.res: They called you a friend, and meant it less.
paranoia.off.favor.2.text: They want you to witness a statement, and to forget the half of it you heard. Sign?
paranoia.off.favor.2.yes.res: Your name is on a document you cannot unsee.
paranoia.off.favor.2.no.res: They signed alone, and wrote your refusal down.
paranoia.off.venture.1.text: A small run of untaxed goods through the Cold Docks: small money, small risk, they say. Take a share?
paranoia.off.venture.1.yes.res: The run came in clean; the next one may not.
paranoia.off.venture.1.no.res: You kept your hands clean and your pockets thin.
paranoia.off.venture.2: Offers a share in forged papers
paranoia.off.venture.2.text: A press for documents is changing hands; the profits are all in other people's names. Put in money?
paranoia.off.venture.2.yes.res: The press runs; you are now a name in a ledger of names.
paranoia.off.venture.2.no.res: You kept out; the press was raided by spring.
paranoia.off.feast.1.text: A feast in the Quiet Ward, with the radio turned up and the curtains drawn. Attend?
paranoia.off.feast.1.yes.res: You ate, and sang, and did not say the wrong thing.
paranoia.off.feast.1.no.res: You stayed in; the gathering was reported.
paranoia.off.feast.2: Invites you to the canteen table
paranoia.off.feast.2.text: The canteen's long table, where the seats face away from the cameras. Take a seat?
paranoia.off.feast.2.yes.res: You found a seat, and a contact, facing the wall.
paranoia.off.feast.2.no.res: You ate alone, facing the lens.
paranoia.off.secret.1: Offers to tell you a secret
paranoia.off.secret.1.text: They want to tell you who filed the report on your father, and why. Listen?
paranoia.off.secret.1.yes.res: Now you know, and knowing is a thing they can kill you for.
paranoia.off.secret.1.no.res: You refused; they respected it, and never came back.
paranoia.off.secret.2: Wants to entrust you a name
paranoia.off.secret.2.text: They want to give you the real name of a disappeared friend, to keep in living memory. Take it?
paranoia.off.secret.2.yes.res: You carry another person's name where the record cannot reach.
paranoia.off.secret.2.no.res: The name went with them into the dark.
paranoia.off.duel.1.text: They accuse you publicly of cowardice, and demand you answer it before the neighbours. Answer?
paranoia.off.duel.1.yes.res: You answered; the crowd believed you, which is itself a danger.
paranoia.off.duel.1.no.res: You walked away, and the whisper followed.
paranoia.off.duel.2.text: Two informers' reports contradict; someone must be lying, and it will be the weaker name. Fight the case?
paranoia.off.duel.2.yes.res: You won; they were transferred to the Sublevels.
paranoia.off.duel.2.no.res: You conceded; your file now says 'unreliable'.
paranoia.off.trade.1.text: Your grandfather's watch, in exchange for a month of not being seen. Make the trade?
paranoia.off.trade.1.yes.res: The watch is gone; the month was silent and sweet.
paranoia.off.trade.1.no.res: You kept the watch and counted the footsteps instead.
paranoia.off.trade.2.text: They can lose your file, if you help lose someone else's. Swap?
paranoia.off.trade.2.yes.res: Your file moved; so did your stomach.
paranoia.off.trade.2.no.res: You refused, and slept on the floor by the door.
paranoia.off.journey.1.text: A crossing of the wire line to a district the Bureau has forgotten; a few nights only. Go?
paranoia.off.journey.1.yes.res: For a few nights you lived where no one knew your name.
paranoia.off.journey.1.no.res: You stayed; the crossing was stopped at dawn.
paranoia.off.journey.2: Asks you to join a work detail
paranoia.off.journey.2.text: A work detail beyond the checkpoint needs one more pair of hands and one more silence. Enlist?
paranoia.off.journey.2.yes.res: You crossed the checkpoint; the far side was emptier.
paranoia.off.journey.2.no.res: You stayed; the detail returned one person short.
paranoia.plugin.desc: The behaviours and pressures by which a city learns to police itself.
